Let's play a game of Four in a Row. You are playing as Black. You will be given the current game state and you will need to give the next move in a standard algebraic notation specific to this game. Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Current player: Black (B)

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Let's play a game of Four in a Row. You are playing as Black. You will be given the current game state and you will need to give the next move in a standard algebraic notation specific to this game. Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Let's play a game of Four in a Row. You are playing as Black. You will be given the current game state and you will need to give the next move in a standard algebraic notation specific to this game. Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Let's play a game of Four in a Row. You are playing as White. You will be given the current game state and you will need to give the next move in a standard algebraic notation specific to this game. Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Let's play a game of Four in a Row. You are playing as White. You will be given the current game state and you will need to give the next move in a standard algebraic notation specific to this game. Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Let's play a game of Four in a Row. You are playing as White. You will be given the current game state and you will need to give the next move in a standard algebraic notation specific to this game. Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

The current board state is:
FEN: 9/9/9/9

Current player: White (W)

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Let's play a game of Four in a Row. You are playing as Black. You will be given the current game state and you will need to give the next move in a standard algebraic notation specific to this game. Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Let's play a game of Four in a Row. You are playing as Black. You will be given the current game state and you will need to give the next move in a standard algebraic notation specific to this game. Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Let's play a game of Four in a Row. You are playing as Black. You will be given the current game state and you will need to give the next move in a standard algebraic notation specific to this game. Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Let's play a game of Four in a Row. You are playing as Black. You will be given the current game state and you will need to give the next move in a standard algebraic notation specific to this game. Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Let's play a game of Four in a Row. You are playing as Black. You will be given the current game state and you will need to give the next move in a standard algebraic notation specific to this game. Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

messages.content:
Let's play a game of Four in a Row. You are playing as White. You will be given the current game state and you will need to give the next move in a standard algebraic notation specific to this game. Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

The current board state is:
FEN: 9/9/9/9

Current player: White (W)

Let's play a game of Four in a Row. You are playing as White. You will be given the current game state and you will need to give the next move in a standard algebraic notation specific to this game. Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

Let's play a game of Four in a Row. You are playing as Black. You will be given the current game state and you will need to give the next move in a standard algebraic notation specific to this game. Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Let's play a game of Four in a Row. You are playing as Black. You will be given the current game state and you will need to give the next move in a standard algebraic notation specific to this game. Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Let's play a game of Four in a Row. You are playing as Black. You will be given the current game state and you will need to give the next move in a standard algebraic notation specific to this game. Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Let's play a game of Four in a Row. You are playing as Black. You will be given the current game state and you will need to give the next move in a standard algebraic notation specific to this game. Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Let's play a game of Four in a Row. You are playing as White. You will be given the current game state and you will need to give the next move in a standard algebraic notation specific to this game. Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Let's play a game of Four in a Row. You are playing as Black. You will be given the current game state and you will need to give the next move in a standard algebraic notation specific to this game. Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Let's play a game of Four in a Row. You are playing as Black. You will be given the current game state and you will need to give the next move in a standard algebraic notation specific to this game. Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

Let's play a game of Four in a Row. You are playing as White. You will be given the current game state and you will need to give the next move in a standard algebraic notation specific to this game. Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:

Let's play a game of Four in a Row. You are playing as White. You will be given the current game state and you will need to give the next move in a standard algebraic notation specific to this game. Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

messages.content:
Let's play a game of Four in a Row. You are playing as Black. You will be given the current game state and you will need to give the next move in a standard algebraic notation specific to this game. Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Let's play a game of Four in a Row. You are playing as Black. You will be given the current game state and you will need to give the next move in a standard algebraic notation specific to this game. Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Let's play a game of Four in a Row. You are playing as Black. You will be given the current game state and you will need to give the next move in a standard algebraic notation specific to this game. Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Let's play a game of Four in a Row. You are playing as Black. You will be given the current game state and you will need to give the next move in a standard algebraic notation specific to this game. Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Let's play a game of Four in a Row. You are playing as Black. You will be given the current game state and you will need to give the next move in a standard algebraic notation specific to this game. Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Let's play a game of Four in a Row. You are playing as White. You will be given the current game state and you will need to give the next move in a standard algebraic notation specific to this game. Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Let's play a game of Four in a Row. You are playing as Black. You will be given the current game state and you will need to give the next move in a standard algebraic notation specific to this game. Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

FEN: 9/4W4/9/9

Current player: Black (B)

Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Let's play a game of Four in a Row. You are playing as Black. You will be given the current game state and you will need to give the next move in a standard algebraic notation specific to this game. Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The game state will be represented in FEN notation, a compact algebraic representation inspired by chess's Forsyth-Edwards Notation. Each row of the 4x9 board is encoded as a string where 'W' represents a White piece, 'B' represents a Black piece, and numbers indicate consecutive empty spaces. Rows are separated by forward slashes ('/'), reading from top to bottom. An empty board is represented as "9/9/9/9", with each '9' indicating that all nine columns in that row are empty.

Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN) Explanation:
Issue moves in the notation m <row> <col>, for example m 0 0 to place your mark in the top leftmost square and m 3 8 to place your mark in the bottom rightmost square.

Let's play a game of Four in a Row. You are playing as Black. You will be given the current game state and you will need to give the next move in a standard algebraic notation specific to this game. Feel free to think about the move, only the final answer you provide in <next_move> </next_move> tags will be played.

Game Rules:
Four in a row is played on a four-by-nine grid by two players, who alternately place the marks W and B in one of the thirty-six spaces in the grid. A player wins when they get four pieces in a row horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Player W plays first.

The standard game state representation is in the following format:
